title: Creating Button hole
content: **Objective ** Create Buttonhole items by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **Required & Recommended** ** ****[Required]** * The buttonhole file format must be *bth. * The image of the buttonhole must have a transparent background and be saved in PNG format. * Buttonhole Images must be black and white with no color value. * Buttonhole Image should not show aliasing. * Buttonhole Image must be registered as horizontal orientation. (Please refer to the example image below.) ![mceclip0.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775727195417) * The DEFAULT SIZE of BUTTONHOLE must be provided in the Description. **[Recommended]** * The image of the buttonhole should be at least 300px in horizontal length. * For stable simulation, make sure the size of the product is not too big or too small. **1\. Create a buttonhole** To save as BTH format, you need to have PNG files having a transparent background. If you have a different format other than PNG, export as a PNG format file from other IMAGE EDITING software. 1\. Open CLO 2\. Move to the Buttonhole Tab and select the buttonhole tab from the Object Browser. ![object_browser.PNG](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775753363481) 3\. To register BUTTONHOLE, click the ‘register’ button next to the Shape menu in PROPERTY EDITOR. ![___1.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775728718489) 4\. Enter registration information ![register.PNG](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775753940889) * **Name.** Enter Product name * **IMAGE**. Click the ‘Open’ button and load IMAGE files to register * For the Thumbnail, Register the thumbnail as landscape orientation with a transparent background and save it in PNG format. ![buttonhole.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775754205465) 5\. Click the ‘**OK** ’ button. **2\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the BTH to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775754525849) **1\. UPLOAD (Mandatory) ** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE (**Mandatory**)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3.****DESCRIPTION** Please provide the default size of the BUTTONHOLE that you created for customers. Please provide the button units or BTH information in Width & Length values. **4\. TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **5\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files relating to the BUTTONHOLE. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. **6\. ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the BTH. **7\. THUMBNAIL** Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the BTH. If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please register the rendered image. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating and uploading buttonhole items using CLO and Marvelous Designer software, detailing required formats, image specifications, and asset registration procedures.

Optimizing the Garment’s Poly Counts** Please optimize the polygon count of the garments to make sure that the created outfit runs without any issues. To optimize the garments' polygon counts, you have several options: **you can adjust the pattern's particle distance value or use EveryWear's 'Polygon Optimization' feature.** Please optimize your outfit with the most convenient option, but not exceed the maximum poly counts listed below. After optimizing the polygon count of the pattern, please also optimize the polygon count of accessories such as buttons, zippers, and trims. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088457497)
```
✔️Double-check if the patterns have been changed to ‘Quad (Optimized).
``` **[Optimize the garment with the ‘Polygon Optimization’ feature]** 1. Open EveryWear * From the main Menu → CONNECT → Open ‘EveryWear.’ 2. Enter the appropriate polygon count in the ‘**Garment Polygons** ’ tab of the Garment tab. 3. Click ‘Optimize.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088462233) 4. Simulate the optimized outfit. ``` 💡Note: How to Adjust Polygon Count for Accessories like Buttons, Zippers, and Trims Using the Optimize function in Polygon Optimization, accessories such as buttons, zippers, and trims may be converted to billboards (planes) during the polygon optimization process. In this case, you can adjust the polygon count for each accessory separately from the patterns by changing the Billboard setting to Mesh in the Property Editor for the respective accessory. Then, enter your preferred value to control the polygon count.
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51683960687001)
```
For buttons or trims that are prominently noticeable, it's recommended to use ‘Mesh’ instead of ‘Billboard’ types. During Polygon Optimization, buttons or trims might be converted to billboards, so it’s advisable to choose the appropriate ‘Mesh Type’ based on the situation.
``` * * * ### **2\. Sealing Openings with Auto Seal** Use the **Auto Seal** function to create capping faces over any openings where the garment’s interior might be exposed—such as hems or sleeve cuffs. This prevents the inside of the garment from showing even when the avatar moves, resulting in a higher‑quality finish. Hidden inner faces are also automatically masked, ensuring that unnecessary internal geometry is not rendered, which improves overall optimization. 1. In the **Garment** tab, open **Polygon Optimization** and click **Auto Seal** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088463897) 2. Create a guide line. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088472217) * **Disk Mode:** In the 3D viewport, click three points on the pattern to generate a disc; the curve formed where the disc intersects the pattern becomes the guide line. * **3D Pen Mode:** Draw a curve directly on the garment (same as the existing 3D Pen tool). Note that the first and last points must meet for the curve to be created. 3. Select the Auto Seal direction. * Using the guide line, choose which side of the new Auto‑Seal face will be exposed. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51682161663001) * In this garment’s case, the sealed face should be oriented downward, so click when the lower portion is highlighted. ``` 💡Auto Seal – Before and After Comparison Image
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510133038489)
```
⚠️ To view the surface generated by Auto Seal in the 3D window, the following two settings must be enabled:
1. 3D Window > Garment Rendering Style > Thick
2. Select Pattern > Geometry > Extrusion Direction > Back Face enabled
If the surface is not visible after using the Auto Seal function, please check that both of the above options are correctly set.
``` * * * ### **3\. Polygon Masking for Hidden Garments** Utilize the ‘**Masking Brush** ’ for additional optimization, such as inner pocket linings or areas hidden by the avatar. For more details, please check the [[Document](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304301912857-Garment-Tab)]. 1. Click the brush icon in the ‘**Polygon Optimization** ’ section under the Garment Tab. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510211598617) 2. Select the appropriate settings in the ‘Masking Brush’ option and use the brush to specify the masking area. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510230841241) * * * ### **4\. Rigging Clothing** Rig the optimized garments to the template avatar’s joints. 1. Click ‘**Apply** ’ in the Rigging option of the EveryWear. (Do not use **Max Influence Joints.**) ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510230842265) ```
⚠️ The ‘Max Influence Joints’ option specifies the maximum number of joints affecting each vertex. The number on the right indicates the ‘Max Influence Joints’ value of the imported avatar. This option is recommended for use only when the ‘Max Influence Joints’ value for the rigged garment needs to be set differently from that of the imported avatar.
```
```
📢 All rigging data will be deleted if you change the design or run a simulation. Therefore, please make sure to rig with the final design.
``` * * * ### **5\. Modifying the Skin Weight of the Clothing** Once rigging is done, click the brush icon to adjust the skin weight and silhouette of the garments. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510279058585) Please refer to the [[Document](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304301912857-Garment-Tab)] or check the [[Tutorial](https://youtu.be/wKjp2Xo0VCQ?si=DDSAWi7oqUpkXg90&t=343)] for more detailed instructions on the brush's weight and sculpt tabs. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510279065497) * * * ### **6\. From the main menu, File → Open → click ‘Joint Motion.’ 2. Import the motion file (.mtn). 3. From the main menu, select **Animation → Animation Editor**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669010585) 4. Slide the ‘Frame Bar’ to check if the garments follow the avatar’s motions appropriately. * Please return to the Skin Weight step to address necessary corrections if adjustments are required. 5. Please refer to the [[Document](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304302920217-Material-Tab)] for more details. 1. Click the ‘**Material Tab** ’ in EveryWear. 2. In the UV Packing section, set the ‘**Image Size(Pixels)** ’ to 2048 and the ‘**Seam Size(Pixels)** ’ to 8. 3. Click ‘**Pack UVs.** ’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510621594009) 4. title: Creating Avatar
content:
**Objective ** Create an Avatar by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **1\. Creating AVATAR** Create an Avatar in other 3D software. Avatar files should be created in OBJ/FBX/GLB/GLTF formats, and avatars with joints are recommended to be in FBX formats. For avatars with textures applied, please make sure to check 'Embed Media' in the Export Option. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775561103897) **※ Note:** The following Skinning Methods are not compatible with CLO and Marvelous Designer: **Dual Quaternion and Weight Blend.** **Required & Recommended** ※ Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling Avatar. ** ****[Required]** * All mesh must be created in Y-axis(up) environment. * You can import the following formats into Avatar Type: OBJ, FBX, GLB, and GLTF. * All mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. **[Recommended]** * For the best outfit-fitting performance, it is strongly recommended to create an avatar in either an A-pose or a T-pose. * If mesh and the normal map have the same location and direction, it may cause overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Be careful not to overlap the mesh. * It is highly recommended to create and apply the avatar's various items, such as shoes, hair, earrings, etc., as separate assets instead of including them in the AVT file. * The scanned data is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. * The number of meshes can impact the speed of CLO, so it is strongly recommended to create an avatar using a maximum of **70,000 triangles.** * Unless you intended to model Avatar asymmetrically, we recommend creating Avatar's mesh and joint symmetrically. * To fully utilize CLO / Marvelous Designer's Avatar IK feature, make sure that the joints' names and structure align with CLO/Marvelous Designer's Avatar. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775497351577) **** **2\. IMPORT AVATAR** Import the avatar files in the following formats into the Avatar Type: OBJ, DAE, FBX, GLTF ![제목 없음-1.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775561384473) **▶ Basic** * Load Type: Open * Object type: Avatar * Scale: Adjust the scale of Avatar. **▶Object** * Camera: Check whether to import camera data or camera animation data. * Joint Animation: Check whether to import animation data. * Cache Animation(MC): Check whether to import Cache Animation (MC) data. **▶Option** * Auto Add Arrangement Points: Automatically generate Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes. * Auto Create Fitting Suit: Automatically generate a Fitting Suit for the avatar. **※ Note:** It is strongly recommended to check 'Auto Add Arrangement Points' and 'Auto Create Fitting Suit' when importing. * Move Garment to Start Position: Adjust the position of the garment to the starting point of the motions. **▶Axis Conversion** : adjust the axis of the Avatar. **▶Translation** * Align Bottom to Ground: Adjust the position of the avatar to be placed on the ground. **▶OK / Cancel** * Press 'OK' to import the Avatar, or press 'Cancel' to re-import the file to be used as the avatar. **3\. Bounding Volume & Arrangement Points ** To dress the garment on the AVATAR, a process called '**Positioning** ' is needed. To carry out the '**Positioning** ' process, it is necessary to generate and modify the BOUNDING VOLUME and ARRANGEMENT POINT. **※ Note:** You can automatically generate both Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points by selecting '**Auto Add Arrangement Points'** during import. **3-1. Creating and Modifying Bounding Volume & Arrangement Points** 1\. from the Main Menu > AVATAR > AVATAR EDITOR 2\. Click **Arrangement Tab** Please refer to the manuals below: * **[Bounding Volume](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000431228-Add-Edit-Bounding-Volume)** * **[Arrangement Point](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000430768-Add-Arrangement-Point)** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775497585945) **4\. FITTING SUIT** The**'Fitting Suit'** is a fitting dummy generated by referring to avatars with various sizes and shapes, enabling automatic dressing by auto-grading garments onto the avatar. **※ Note:** You can automatically generate a fitting suit by selecting **'Auto Create Fitting Suit'** during import. If the **'Fitting Suit'** is not positioned correctly, please generate it manually. **4-1. Creating Fitting Suit** 1\. From the Main Menu > AVATAR > AVATAR EDITOR 2\. Click **FITTING SUIT Tab** Please refer to the manuals below: * **[Fitting Suit](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/24451580024601-Create-the-Avatar-Fitting-Suit-ver-7-3)** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775513153689) **5\. Modifying AVATAR's Material** If you want to modify the textures and materials applied to AVATAR, you can adjust them in the Property Editor. 1\. Click the Avatar (AVT) in 3D Window 2\. Apply the textures and materials in the Property Editor. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775529091481) **6\. Save as AVT** Save the AVT file with both textures and materials applied. 1\. from the Main Menu, File > Save As > AVATAR ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775529415065) 2\. After specifying the file name and directory path, click Save (S). **7\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the AVT to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775555464985) **1\. UPLOAD****(Mandatory)**** ** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE****(Mandatory)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3.****DESCRIPTION** please specify the following information on the Avatar file (AVT). * AVATAR HEIGHT (Scale Unit) * BUST CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * HIP CIRCUMFERENCE (Scale Unit) * Presence of the JOINTS * Availability / Unavailability of CLO's AVATAR SIZING EDITOR * Compatibility / Incompatibility with CLO's default avatar ASSETS * Presence of the Magic Suit's Application Status **4\. title: Referral Not Applied: Cases & Restrictions
content: ### How the Referral Feature Works When a friend enters CONNECT using your referral link, the referrer’s information is stored in the web browser’s cookies. ### When a Referral Cannot Be Established A referral relationship will **not** be created in the following cases: * A friend initially entered through one referrer’s link, but later signed up or made a purchase through another referrer’s link. * A friend enters through the referrer’s link but later uses a **different browser to purchase.** * A friend **deletes cookies** after entering through the referrer’s link. * Any other situation where the cookie-stored information cannot be retrieved. ### Prohibited Activities in Referral Programs The following actions are strictly prohibited while participating in the referral program: * Create a website that pretends to be CONNECT or replicates its design. * Share your referral link on illegal or unsafe websites. * Do anything that harms CONNECT’s reputation or brand image. * Use or share content that violates someone else’s copyright or the law. * Use illegal or unauthorized software that infringes CLO or Marvelous Designer’s rights. ### Losing Referrer Eligibility * Referrers who violate these policies will lose their eligibility. * Any earnings generated **after** losing eligibility will **not** be recognized.
content_description: Learn how to effectively use the referral feature while understanding the rules and restrictions to maintain your eligibility and protect CONNECT's integrity.

title: Referral Earnings Payout
content: ### When You Receive Earnings * Referral earnings are paid **the month after a sale occurs** , just like item sales. * For example, if a friend makes a purchase in January, your referral earnings will be paid at the **end of February**. * If an item is refunded, the earnings from that order will **not** be included. ### Minimum Payout Amount * Referral earnings are paid once your total earnings reach **$10 or more**.**(This calculation is based solely on referral earnings and is separate from item sales revenue.)** * Earnings below $10 will **accumulate** , and you will receive a payout in the month your total earnings reach $10 or more. ### How to Receive Your Earnings Earnings are automatically recorded, but you need to provide **payout information** to receive them. * Sellers who have already provided payout information for item sales **do not need to enter it again** — earnings will be paid automatically. * If you haven’t provided payout information yet, please follow the instructions below to register your **seller/payout information**. [Seller Info Registration](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/sections/44750777753497--Seller-Info-Registration)
content_description: This page outlines the process for receiving referral earnings, including payout timing, minimum payout thresholds, and instructions for submitting payout information.

title: Referral Earnings Status
content: ### When Do You Receive Referral Earnings? If a friend signs up through your referral link or makes their first paid purchase through your shared link, a **referral relationship** is established. If that friend then makes **any paid purchase within 60 days** of establishing the referral relationship, **10% of the purchase amount** will be credited to you as referral earnings. ### How to Check Your Referral Earnings 1. Click your **profile menu** on the right in CONNECT. 2. Click the **Sales** menu. 3. Select the **Referral** tab at the top. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/52811384718617) 4\. Under **Referral** , choose either the **Order** or **Payout** tab to view earnings by item. > Make sure the **date range** is set correctly when checking your referral earnings. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/52811384719257) #### **Checking Your Referral Status** You can find information about friends you have a referral relationship with and items sold during the selected period. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/52811429670169) **Invited Friends** * The number of friends with an active referral relationship during the selected period. * A friend is counted if **any part of their 60-day referral period** falls within the selected dates. **Items** * The total number of items purchased by your referred friends during the selected period. **Referral Revenue** * The total referral earnings for the selected period. * This equals **10% of the sales amount** of items purchased by your referred friends.
content_description: Discover how to track and maximize your referral earnings from friends who sign up or make purchases through your unique referral link.

title: How the Referral Program Works - First Paid
content: #### **Eligible Referrals** * Friends who are registered but have never purchased a paid item. **(Existing User, no paid purchases)** #### **Establishing a Referral Relationship** * It can also begin when a friend who is already registered—but has never purchased a paid item—makes their first paid purchase through your shared link. * Once the referral relationship is established, it remains in effect for **60 days**. During this period, you’ll earn **10% of the friend’s total purchase amount** as your referral reward. #### **Referral Scenarios** **1)********First Paid Purchase:** When a new friend (Referee N), who is not registered, signs up on CONNECT using the link shared by an existing user (Referrer R), a referral relationship is established. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026457843225) **2)****Multiple Invitations:** Referee N may receive links from multiple Referrers, but **no referral relationship is established until they sign up**. If multiple Referrers send links, the referral relationship is **established only with the Referrer whose link the Referee used to sign up**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026457845913) **3) After Referral is Established:** Once the referral relationship is established, receiving additional links from other referrers **will not change the existing relationship**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026441168025) **4)****Earnings During Referral:** During the 60-day referral period, **10% of all paid purchases made by the friend(referree)** is credited to the referrer. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026441169177) **5)** **Referral Duration:** After 60 days, the referral relationship ends, and purchases made by the friend(referee) **will no longer be credited to the referrer.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53026457856537)

title: Reviewing the Checklist before Export
content: Before exporting your clothing, make sure to review the checklist below to confirm that nothing has been missed. * * * **✔️Check List** * Check whether the mesh type of the pattern has been changed to **‘Quad(Optimized).’** * Check the garments do not exceed the **maximum polygon counts.** * Make sure that your clothing does not have any issues with rigging during the skinning test motion. * Ensure the garment is created as a **“Thickness”** type. * Verify that every opening where the interior could be exposed—such as at sleeve cuffs or the hem—is sealed. * Check if there are any areas where the clothing mesh is flipped. * After the garment has been fully completed, including rigging and all related processes, please make sure the avatar is set to the default pose. * Check that the **Seam Face** option is set to **Off** for all patterns. * Check that the garment, when viewed from various angles, exhibits no see-through issues.

title: Step 4: FAQ
content: ### **📋****Basic Questions** **Question: Where can I find the VRChat avatar/clothing/accessory creation guide?** Answer: <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/> **Question: How do I install Modular Avatar?** Answer: Please refer to the official Modular Avatar documentation: <https://modular-avatar.nadena.dev/> **Question: Where can I download Unity and VRChat SDK?** Answer: * Unity Hub: <https://unity.com/download> * VRChat Creator Companion (VCC): <https://vcc.docs.vrchat.com/> **Question: Must I use Unity version 2022.3.22f1?** Answer: Use a Unity version compatible with VRChat SDK 3.5.2+. The latest version can be confirmed in the official VRChat documentation. 🔗 <https://creators.vrchat.com/sdk/upgrade/current-unity-version/> **Question: Can I use a different workflow?** Answer: Yes, but you must provide a detailed guide for buyers. **Requirements:** * Step-by-step installation method * Include screenshots * FAQ and troubleshooting methods * * * ### **🔧 Unity Package Related** **Question: What if my Unity Package exceeds 1GB?** Answer: Adjust texture resolution or remove unnecessary files. Main methods: * Reduce texture resolution (2048→1024) * Delete unused Blendshapes * Remove hidden polygons * Optimize materials **Question: Should I check 'Include dependencies' when exporting Unity Package?** Answer: Yes, you must check it. If unchecked, necessary Shaders or Materials may be missing. * * * ### **📊 Polygon & Performance Rank** **Question: What is the recommended polygon count for VRChat avatars?** Answer: * **PC:** 70,000 triangles or less (Good Rank standard) * **Quest:** 20,000 triangles or less (required) ⚠️ Exceeding 70,000 triangles will drop the rating to 'Very Poor'. 💡Related Documentation * **Performance Ranks (Official Documentation)** 🔗 <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-performance-ranking-system/> * **Avatar Optimization Tips (Official Documentation)** 🔗 <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-optimizing-tips/> **Question: If Performance Rank is 'Very Poor', can I still sell it?** Answer: Yes, sales are permitted. It is common for popular avatars across various marketplaces to have a 'Very Poor' rating. While CONNECT does not impose restrictions based on Performance Rank, please note that buyers may prefer optimized avatars. **Question: Where can I check polygon count?** Answer: In Unity, check at `VRChat SDK Control Panel → Avatar Stats`. * * * ### **🎨 Shader & Material** **Question: My avatar/clothing displays in pink.** Answer: Shader is missing. Solution: 1. Import required Shaders (lilToon, Poiyomi, etc.) **before** importing Unity Package 2. If Shader is already installed, reassign the Material **Question: My avatar/clothing displays in white.** Answer: Material is not applied. Solution: 1. Find the Material and assign it to the avatar's Mesh Renderer 2. Or drag and drop the Material directly onto the avatar part * * * ### **💨 PhysBone Related** **Question: PhysBone doesn't work in-game.** Answer: Please check the following: 1. Verify VRChat SDK is the latest version (update via VRChat Creator Companion) 2. Verify PhysBone component is assigned to the correct bone 3. Recheck after test upload to VRChat **Question: PhysBone Transform Count error occurs.** Answer: Too many PhysBones. Solution: 1. Delete unnecessary PhysBones 2. Add End Bone to 'Ignore Transforms' 3. PhysBone count limits: * PC: No limit (but consider performance) * Quest: Maximum 8 PhysBone components, 64 affected transforms **Question: Cannot set PhysBone on End Bone.** Answer: Error occurs if the end bone is branched. Solution: * Add endpoint bone using Endpoint Position * * * ### **📤 Upload & Sales** **Question: How do I test upload to VRChat?** Answer: In Unity: `VRChat SDK → Show Control Panel → Build & Test` **Question: What files should I include in Unity Package?** Answer: * **Required:** Prefab, FBX, Textures, Materials, etc. - files used in item creation * **Recommended:** ReadMe.txt, usage guide * **Optional:** .blend, .psd (source files)

For guidance on the basic creation process, please refer to the official VRChat guides below. **VRChat Official Guides** 🔗**VRChat Creators Main:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/> 🔗**VRChat Avatar Guide:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/> 🔗**Creating Your First Avatar:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/creating-your-first-avatar/> **VRChat Performance Rank Reference** We recommend creating items with the total polygon count (avatar body + clothing + accessories, etc.) according to the following platform-specific standards: * **PC - Good Rank Recommended Standard** : Total polygon count of 70,000 triangles or less * Quest compatibility: Total polygon count of 20,000 triangles or less 🔗**Performance Ranks:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-performance-ranking-system/> 🔗**Avatar Optimization Tips:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-optimizing-tips/> 🔗**Android Content Optimization (Quest):** <https://creators.vrchat.com/platforms/android/quest-content-optimization/> * * * Below are the essential and recommended settings for each item type: ### **2-1. Avatar Creation** **Essential Settings** * **Humanoid Rig Setup** * **Add VRC Avatar Descriptor Component** * View Position Setup (viewpoint position in VRChat - recommended between both eyes) * Avatar Size **(Humanoid standard)** : 0.5~5m (average 1.65m) * Exceeding this range may cause IK operation errors in VRChat. **Recommended Settings** * **Eye Bone:** For eye movement simulation * **Viseme:** Recommended for mouth shape setup (Blendshape method recommended) * **PhysBone:** For physics effects on hair/tail, etc. * **Blendshape:** For facial expressions and appearance changes * Please optimize the avatar's polygon count so buyers can combine various clothing/accessories. ### **2-2. Clothing Creation** **Essential Information** * **Specify Compatible Avatar** * Please clearly indicate the avatar name(s) that the clothing is compatible with in the description so buyers can confirm (e.g., Lucy) * We recommend including the avatar's sales link for easy buyer verification. * **Specify Clothing Polygon Count** * Please list the total polygon count of the clothing in the description so buyers can confirm. * Use Triangle standard for specification (e.g., +8,500 Triangles) * We recommend minimizing polygons so buyers can combine with other items. **Recommended Settings** * **PhysBone Setup** * We recommend adding PhysBone to parts that need movement, such as skirts or capes, to add swaying effects. * Excessive PhysBone can cause performance degradation, so please use only where necessary. * For Quest compatibility, we recommend minimizing PhysBone usage. * **Penetration Prevention** * Please minimize clothing clipping through the avatar's body. * Pay special attention to arms, chest, and thigh areas as they have significant movement, and we recommend testing with various body types and poses. * **Remove Unnecessary Polygons** * Please delete hidden avatar body parts under clothing (e.g., torso and arms not visible when wearing a top). * Removing internal clothing faces and invisible details will reduce unnecessary polygons and improve performance. * **Quest Optimization** * For Quest platform compatibility, we recommend consolidating Materials into one. ### **2-3. Accessory Creation** **Essential Information** * **Specify Compatible Avatar** * Please clearly indicate the avatar name(s) that the accessory is compatible with in the description so buyers can confirm (e.g., Lucy) * We recommend including the avatar's sales link for easy buyer verification. * **Specify Accessory Polygon Count** * Please list the total polygon count of the accessory in the description so buyers can confirm. * Use Triangle standard for specification (e.g., +3,200 Triangles) * We recommend minimizing polygons so buyers can combine with other items. * **Specify Attachment Location** * Please specify where the accessory attaches (e.g., Head, Hand, Back, Chest, etc.) **Recommended Settings** * **PhysBone Setup** * We recommend adding PhysBone to parts that need movement, such as earrings or tail accessories, to add swaying effects. * Excessive PhysBone can cause performance degradation, so please use only where necessary. * For Quest compatibility, we recommend minimizing PhysBone usage. * **Attachment Location Considerations** * **Head:** Please position so it doesn't obstruct vision. Especially earrings, hats, etc. need verification from first-person perspective. * **Hand:** Please configure to accurately match hand bone positions. Testing is needed to ensure natural appearance during hand movements. * **Back** : Please verify no clipping through avatar body or floor when sitting or lying down. * **Chest:** We recommend allowing tolerance to accommodate chest size variations. * **Consider Multiple Accessory Combinations** * Since buyers often wear multiple accessories simultaneously, please minimize individual accessory polygons and Materials. * For example, we recommend creating each accessory lightweight so earrings, necklaces, bracelets, bags, etc. can be worn together. * **Quest Optimization** * For Quest platform compatibility, we recommend consolidating Materials into one. * * * ### **📦 Unity Package Export** After completing production, create a Unity Package. **Export Steps:** 1. Select the folder/files to upload in the Project window 2. Top menu: `Assets` → `Export Package...` 1. **Required Check:** ☑️ `Include dependencies` 3. Select save path and click save button **Notes:** * **Maximum file capacity: 1GB** * Verify all essential assets are included (Prefab, Textures, Materials, Meshes, etc.) * Do not include SDK or Modular Avatar itself (buyers install separately) **Reference:** [Unity Package Official Guide](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/AssetPackages.html) * * * ### **✅ CONNECT Recommended Production Method** CONNECT recommends the following production method to enable buyers to use items easily and quickly: **1\. Provide as Unity Package** * `.unitypackage` format * Maximum capacity: 1GB * Include all assets (Prefab, Textures, Materials, Meshes, etc.) **2\. Include Prefab** * Provide in Prefab format so buyers can use it immediately by dragging and dropping onto the avatar * Reference: [Unity Prefab Guide](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/Prefabs.html) **3\. Modular Avatar Compatible Structure** * **Rigged Items** (clothing, long tails, wings, etc.): * Must include bone structure * Bone names must match the target avatar * Mesh must be properly skinned * **Non-Rigged Accessories** (hats, glasses, etc.): * Provide in Prefab format positioned appropriately for easy buyer placement For details: [Modular Avatar Official Documentation](https://modular-avatar.nadena.dev/docs/intro), [Clothing Compatibility Guide](https://modular-avatar.nadena.dev/docs/tutorials/clothing) **4\. Include Basic Information in Item Description** * Compatible avatar list * Simple installation/usage instructions (e.g., "Apply using Modular Avatar") * Required tools (Unity version, VRChat SDK, Modular Avatar, etc.) * * * ### **⚠️ If Using a Different Production Method** If using a different method than the recommended production method above, please **specify the usage guide in the Description** for buyers: **Recommended Inclusions:** * Basic installation method * Compatible avatar list * Required tools/assets (e.g., specific Shader, VRCFury, etc.) * FAQ (optional) **Providing a detailed guide is optional but recommended:** * Step-by-step installation method (including screenshots) * Format: PDF, Notion/Google Docs link, or ReadMe.txt

title: Creating Zipper Puller
content: **Zipper Structure** **![mceclip0.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775813072665)** **Puller** ※ Please check the requirements and recommendations for the Puller below. **[Required]** * The puller(zipper) file format must be *ZPL or *ZPU. * Only files in OBJ format are supported for registration as a Puller, and the OBJ should only contain the Puller Mesh. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3 (100%). Please create the Puller file(OBJ) in size #3. * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Place the puller on the slider to the origin (0,0,0). * In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status **[Recommended]** * If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. * If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. * For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. **(e.g. logo,****pattern, etc.)** * It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 1024 pixels. * The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. * It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. * you can't apply multiple materials to a puller but can render various materials using textures. Therefore, it's essential to have UV unwrapping done in a way that textures can be created without overlapping. ![Puller.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775845186585) <Puller Mesh's Position on the Grid> **1\. Puller Registration ** **1\. Open CLO S/W** **2\. Register OBJ from the Main Menu > Material > Zipper > Register OBJ** ![puller_registration.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775813586201) **▶Basic** * **Type** : Puller * **Name** : Enter the name of the file to be created. * **Scale** : Select the same scale unit when creating the OBJ. * **Axis Convention** : Set up the axis so the Zipper can be positioned properly.** ** **▶File**** ** * **OBJ** : Import the OBJ file to be registered. **▶Preview :** Check the imported Puller file in advance. **▶OK/Cancel : Click OK to finish the file creation when the file registration is done.** _**The created file is saved in each object folder as**Assets > Materials > Hardware_and_Trims > Zipper. ****_ **2\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the ZPL to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775796851225) **1\. UPLOAD (Mandatory) ** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE (**Mandatory**)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3.****DESCRIPTION** Please provide the default size of the ZPL that you created for customers. Please provide the ZPL information referencing the Property Editor in CLO / Marvelous Designer. * Gauge * % * Weight (g) **4\. TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **5\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files relating to the ZPL. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. **6\. ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the ZPL. **7\. THUMBNAIL** Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the ZPL. If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please register the rendered image. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.

title: Creating Button
content: **Objective ** Create Button items by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **Required & Recommended** ** ****[Required]** * The mesh’s normal direction should be facing outwards. * The point where the OBJ button will be anchored to the garment must be placed at the origin (0,0,0). * In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status **[Recommended]** * Button OBJs should be made with less than 10,000 triangles, so there is no speed problem in CLO software simulation. * UVs should be unwrapped to prevent overlapping, enabling users to apply a variety of textures without issues. * In the case of a button with a thread, the thread mesh must be named 'Ren_Thread' to separate the button and thread from the CLO software Material. (**To create BTN file by THREAD TYPE** for reference) * If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. * If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. * please use the Normal map for the complex graphic pattern. **(e.g. logo, pattern, etc.)** * It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 512 pixels. * The scanned data is compatible, but the mesh should be meshed and editable. * It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. **1\. Checking the Direction and Position of the Button OBJ** Please import the button OBJ into CLO to make sure that the position and direction of the Button OBJ are correctly set, before registering the button. ▶ Mesh Image with the correct position and orientation ![9.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775648586265) ▶ Mesh Image with the wrong position and orientation ![10.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775657605017) **2\. Converting BTN format in CLO software:** Only CLO-formatted files can be uploaded to CONNECT. All buttons must be saved in BTN format in CLO software. To save in BTN format, you need to have OBJ files. If you have a different format other than OBJ, export it as an OBJ format file from other 3D MODELING software. 2-1. Open CLO 2-2. Move to the Button Tab and select the button tab from the Object Browser. ![mceclip0.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775617133721) 2-3. To register BUTTON, click the ‘register’ button next to the Shape menu in PROPERTY EDITOR. 2-4. Enter registration information ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775658081305) **1\. Name** : Enter the name of the BTN to be sold. 2\. If the OBJ files differ for each button size, click the '+' button beside tab '1' to register buttons of various sizes. **3\. OBJ** : Load the OBJ to be registered as a button. * Select Mesh: Check the mesh corresponding to buttons and threads in the OBJ file. The selected Mesh will be highlighted in yellow in the Preview window. **4\. Specification** * Width(mm): Width of the button * Thickness(mm): Thickness of the button * Weight(g): Weight of the button **5\. Set as Default:** Set as the default size for the BTN. * **'Set as Default'** is always checked when creating a single button. * Make sure to check it in the file that you intend to set as the default size if you are creating multiple sizes. **6\. Axis Conversion:** adjust the axis of the OBJ in real-time. **7\. Preview:** Preview the imported OBJ button. **8. Click the ‘OK’ button** **3\. Modifying the material of the BUTTON** 2-1. Modify the Button's properties: You may adjust the material and properties of BTN in the Property Editor. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775634024089) **▶ Name.** Modify the name of the button as needed. **▶ Shape. **Adjust the size, thickness, and weight of the BUTTON. modifications are possible if the specification is 'Custom.' On the other hand, for the Size Button, modifications are not allowed. **▶ Material. **Select the BUTTON's material, Color, and Texture from the Type Option. 3-2. Click the SAVE button in the PROPERTY EDITOR, to save it in BTN format. **4\. creating THREAD TYPE BTN** * CLO SOFTWARE provides functionality that allows you to edit the visible THREAD when securing BUTTON. * **CROSS** , **PARALLEL** , and **SQUARE** are three THREAD TYPES that can be created. To utilize the Thread Type feature, it is essential to have all three types of *.BTN files: **Cross** , **Parallel** , and **Square**. * For button files utilizing the Thread Type feature, add **'_Cross,' '_Parallel,' and '_Square'** to the file name after OBJ. This naming convention applies only to the Button OBJ files using the Thread Type feature. ![mceclip5.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775658484633) 4-2. Generate the OBJ files for THREAD TYPE in step 4-1. \- Make sure that the names of OBJ files for each THREAD TYPE are set as ***_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj.** 4-3. Create BTN files from previously generated OBJ files. ![mceclip8.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775666577945) 4-4. Save the generated *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn, and *_Square.btn files to the following path: **C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\Assets\Materials\Hardware_and_Trims\Button & Buttonhole\Button.** 4-5. Run CLO and adjust the Button's Thread Type in the Property Editor under Shape> Thread Type. **5\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the BTN to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775666873241) **1\. TITLE (**Mandatory**)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT.
